summary: CDN mirror rewrites Set-Cookie attributes causing loss of tenant pin and routing to canary
description:
Issue summary:
Satori Health reports intermittent requests being routed to a canary variant despite an explicit tenant model pin. The problem began after the customer enabled traffic mirroring for a low-traffic canary. A subset (~0.6%) of their production requests lose model affinity and receive responses from the canary model, causing user-visible changes in outputs and a billing delta.
Impact:
- ~0.6% of requests for Satori Health served incorrect (canary) model outputs for pinned routes.
- Affected flows are stateful streaming sessions where clients rely on model stability.
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity; immediate mitigation requested.
Environment:
- prod:us-east-1, Dedicated pool id: dp-1983
- Ingress path uses customer's CDN (edge-config v2.7) + Redwood edge-adapter behind it.
- Canary mirroring configured with 0.5% mirror rate via control plane slice id slice-20260309-5
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer enables mirroring to canary variant (slice-20260309-5) at 0.5%
2) Send long streaming session with chunked requests and large initial system prompt (15k chars)
3) Observe Set-Cookie header from our origin; CDN rewrites attributes and returns altered cookie to client
4) After 3–7 minutes of session activity, some requests from same tenant are routed to canary variant instead of pinned model
logs:
Samples (redacted):
- request_id=req-20260310-0a4b, tenant=satori-prod, edge-recv: cookie=pin=rw-internal%2Flongform-2.1; Path=/api/v1; SameSite=None; Secure
- edge-send->origin header: cookie=pin=rw-internal%2Flongform-2.1; Path=/api/v1; Secure
- cdn-returned-set-cookie: pin=rw-internal%2Flongform-2.1; Path=/; SameSite=Lax; HttpOnly
- routing-coordinator decision log: req-req-0a4b -> variant=canary (reason: no pin cookie found, fallback routing)
Control plane snapshot ids: cplane-snap-20260310-08, orchestrator-epoch: 4139
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: routing-coordinator lost cookie-based affinity when CDN mutated Set-Cookie attributes.
What we checked:
- Edge-adapter logs show Set-Cookie from origin present and correct.
- CDN (customer-managed) introduced a rewrite rule last week to normalize cookie paths and SameSite defaults to 'Lax' for security hardening (change id cdn-rule-20260301-7).
- When CDN rewrites Path and SameSite, the client cookie returned to the origin had a different scope (Path=/ instead of Path=/api/v1) and often dropped HttpOnly flag; the routing-coordinator's cookie parser ignores cookies without expected path/scope and treats tenant as unpinned.
- Reproduction on staging with the customer's CDN reproduction fixture: toggling the CDN rule reproduces the loss of pin within 2–5 minutes for streaming sessions with multiple sub-requests.
- No evidence of orchestrator snapshot corruption; control plane consistently reported pin intent for tenant during events.
- Correlated traffic spikes: batches with chunked multi-part uploads increased header compression at CDN causing intermittent header truncation; this increased the chance the mutated Set-Cookie reached clients in the altered form.
- Related Slack thread: #support / messages link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0SUPP/0243 (internal discussion).
root_cause_summary: Customer-managed CDN rule rewrites Set-Cookie attributes (Path and SameSite) and in some cases truncates headers during compressed multi-part requests. The routing-coordinator relies on cookie path and exact attribute matching to maintain model pin. When the cookie's path does not match '/api/v1' or SameSite is changed, the cookie parser rejects the pin and fallback routing selects the canary. This is a compatibility gap between edge cookie normalization and our pinning heuristics.
temporary_workaround:
1) Customer rolled back the CDN cookie-normalization rule (cdn-rule-20260301-7) — immediate reduction in incidents observed.
2) We advised customer to disable mirroring for the affected route as a stop-gap.
3) Engineering suggested a client-side mitigation: set explicit cookie path attribute (Path=/api/v1) for pin cookie in origin responses until permanent fix is deployed.
Note: rollback requires CDN propagation (~10–15 min) and was coordinated via customer SRE.
fix_plan:
Short term (next 24h):
- Push hotfix to routing-coordinator cookie parser to accept pins that match on tenant token header when cookie path is broader (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1456).
- Add defensive logic to fall back to per-request 'x-tenant-pin' header if present and authoritative.
Long term (2–3 sprints):
- Improve pin discovery to be resilient to cookie attribute mutations (path-insensitive match with explicit pin TTL enforcement).
- Add telemetry and alerts for 'cookie-attr-mutation' events in edge-adapter.
- Update onboarding docs to include recommended CDN rules for Dedicated customers.
Owner: Liam Chen; ETA for hotfix deploy: 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC.

2026-03-10 15:04 - Liam Chen: Initial triage indicates edge cookie mutation. Requested the customer to disable mirroring for the pinned route; they accepted and observed partial improvement.
2026-03-11 09:20 - SRE (Marcus Holt): Confirmed CDN rule cdn-rule-20260301-7 present; reproduced header rewrite in customer's staging fixture. Adding SRE to coordinate rollback.
2026-03-11 14:35 - Liam Chen: Submitted routing hotfix PR to accept header pin fallback. Running CI and integration tests against dedicated pool simulator.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: customer rolled back CDN rule and disabled mirroring while we validated hotfix. Hotfix (PR #1456) merged and deployed to canaries in prod:us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 17:45 UTC. Post-deploy observations show dropped incidents from ~0.6% to <0.01% for Satori Health.
Follow-ups: update customer onboarding docs, schedule a compatibility runbook with Satori SRE to validate CDN rules for other routes, and implement long-term path-insensitive pin matching (tracked as engineering story INT-2027).
